To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
considerable numbers of resting and activated lymphocytes of distinct subpopulations are transmitted by human liver graft and may be of clinical relevance after transplantation.
considerable numbers of lymphocytes, predominantly activated T cells, are regularly transmitted to recipients with human liver grafts.
considerable numbers of lymphocytes of distinct phenotypes are regularly transmitted by human liver graft to the recipient, and may be of relevance after transplantation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of whether the transferred donor cells may contribute to the immunological defense against viral and bacterial infections, or may even play a role in the rejection process.
the question, whether donor lymphocytes are transferred to the recipient with the liver transplant and, if this is the case, which cells are involved and what is their phenotype.
the study of lymphocytes transferred from the donor to the recipient by the liver graft and their potential function after transplantation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the presence of donor lymphocytes in the liver allograft is not a rare event but is a common finding in human orthotopic liver transplantation.
the liver allograft is a source of passenger lymphocytes, which are transferred with the organ.
lymphocytes are transferred by human liver graft and may be relevant after transplantation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the liver contains a substantial amount of lymphocytes which can be transferred to the recipients by the grafts.
the liver contains a large amount of donor T cells and that these cells may have the ability to induce graft rejection.
the number of donor lymphocytes transmitted to the recipient is sufficient to induce graft versus host disease.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the number of donor lymphocytes transmitted by human liver graft is substantial.
there is a potential for donor T cells to be transferred to the liver graft recipient, and this is likely to have some impact on the outcome of the transplant.
there is an important role of donor lymphocytes in the immune reconstitution of the patient after liver transplantation.
